_comment: Measured locally with `bazel --nohome_rc run --test_sharding_strategy=disabled
--run_under=//tools/bazel:test_env //cmd/bd:bd_proxied_test -- -test.parallel=1
-test.v=test2json -test.v` (local sandboxed execution only; no remote executor
or cache flags were configured for any measurement run).
Primary source: a single fresh, manifest-aligned 30-shard sweep where every
shard ran its exact assigned test set once (no duplicates, no gaps -- see
scripts/ci/gen_proxied_shard_manifest.py's exact-once coverage check). For
each shard's test.xml, a top-level test's measured time is its own
<testsuite time=...> attribute (the whole top-level Go test's wall-clock,
including setup/teardown and any parallel subtests) when errors="0" -- a
JUnit suite with errors="0" ran to completion even if some of its subtests
FAILED, so failing-but-complete suites are still usable, trustworthy duration
data. errors>0 means the suite was still in flight when Go's test-level
timeout fired and is excluded (treated as no data).
A handful of tests (the sweep's heaviest/slowest, which bump into Bazel's
per-target 15-minute default test timeout even running alone) had no
complete top-level <testsuite time> and were re-measured individually via
`bazel run` (which has no fixed per-test timeout and emits no JUnit XML).
For these, the duration is a leaf-subtest-only sum of that log's
`--- PASS/FAIL: name (Ns)` lines: an entry is included only when no other
entry's name starts with "<name>/", i.e. only leaves of the subtest tree
are summed, so a parent group's line (whose own duration already reflects,
not adds to, its parallel children's wall-clock time) is never added on top
of its children's times. An earlier pass at this file double-counted by
summing every PASS/FAIL line indiscriminately, inflating parallel-subtest
groups by including both parent and child durations; this file corrects that.
Every re-measurement was taken with no other heavy bazel/dolt job running
concurrently on the box. A first attempt at re-measuring stragglers
overlapped in wall-clock time with a second, unrelated heavy sweep and its
numbers came out 2-3x inflated versus the same tests measured cleanly
(confirmed by direct comparison for TestProxiedServerUpdate and
TestProxiedServerLink, which did NOT need re-measurement in the end because
the clean full sweep already had good data for them); that contaminated
data was discarded and is not reflected here.
TestProxiedServerDep2 was re-measured in full isolation and initially
appeared possibly hung (15+ minutes with no new PASS/FAIL lines and no CPU
growth in the top-level test-binary process); it was not a hang, it simply
finished slowly -- each of its subtests does a full `bd init --proxied-server`
against a real dolt server, so wall-clock work happens in short-lived child
processes rather than the parent test binary, and Go buffers an entire
parallel subtest group's PASS/FAIL lines until the group's last member
finishes (confirmed separately for TestProxiedServerClose, whose own long
silent stretch resolved the same way). Letting it run to completion
(2357.72s total) rather than guessing or faking a value avoided reporting
bad data here.
`seconds_per_init_fallback` is the weighted average seconds-per-init over
every measured test in this file (sum of all durations / sum of all inits),
used only for a brand-new test with no entry yet (see
scripts/ci/gen_proxied_shard_manifest.py's discover_inits_cost()).
This file intentionally no longer claims shard totals land "within 5s" of
each other -- see .github/workflows/bazel.yml for the current, honest
expected spread for the 30-shard proxied lane.
Regenerate with a local `bazel --nohome_rc run --test_sharding_strategy=disabled
--run_under=//tools/bazel:test_env //cmd/bd:bd_proxied_test --
-test.parallel=1 -test.v=test2json -test.v` sweep (or a manifest-aligned
sharded sweep per shard) -- not from downloaded CI artifacts -- so the
exact-once leaf-summation methodology above can be applied consistently.
